PC: Resident performs and communicates a reliable, comprehensive history and physical exam (PC2)
Resident determines the necessity of diagnostic studies (PC 3)
Resident consistently asks patients for drug allergies (PC5)
Resident recognizes the need for patient re-evaluation (PC6)
Appropriately order oxygen, monitor and IV access on a ill patient
Recognize anaphylaxis and initiate appropriate treatment including epinephrine (0.3mg 1/1000 IM).
Recognize the need for repeat epinephrine IM injection when patient with anaphylaxis has recurrent symptoms
MK: Resident constructs a list of potential diagnosis based on chief complaint and initial assessment (PC4)
Resident knows the different classifications of pharmacologic agents and their mechanism of action. (PC5)
Describe an approach to a critically ill patient in the ED including assessment of the airway, breathing and circulation
SBP: Resident can describes basic resources available for the care of patients in the Emergency Department (ie. Appropriate dispo/consults) (PC7)
Resident can manage a single patient amid distractions (PC8)
ICS: Resident establishes rapport with and demonstrate empathy toward patients and their families (ICS1)
Resident listens effectively to patients and their families (ICS1)
Resident participates as a member of a patient care team (ICS2)
PROF: Resident demonstrates behavior that conveys caring, honesty, genuine interest and tolerance when interacting with a diverse population of patients and families
